archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (shot-suppression)
archetype.definition: A Detroit team that, for the first time in this stretch of seasons, is breaking even or better on 5-on-5 chances and shots, but sits below .500 because it cannot finish, one of its goalies has been well below average and its penalty kill leaks.

report.headline: Detroit finally controls play; finishing, Gibson and the kill are sinking it
report.take:
Detroit's 8-10-3 record and 23rd-place site rank look like more of the same from a franchise that has finished between 19th and 27th on this site every year since 2021-22. Underneath, this is a different team. The Red Wings hold 50.8% of 5-on-5 expected goals and an even 50% of shot attempts. In every one of the last five seasons they were under 49% in expected goals, with lows of 45.9% and 46.2%. They also allow only 24.4 shots a game, 4th-fewest in the league, while generating 28.5, which is 10th. Few teams below .500 can say that about their territorial game.

The record comes from three leaks. The first is finishing. Detroit's skaters are shooting 9.2% in all situations, 30th in the league against an 11.4% average, so a top-10 shot volume turns into the 28th-ranked 2.71 goals a game. The second is the crease, which is really two goalies. Daniil Tarasov has a .931 save %, +9.5 GSAx and two shutouts, and he ranks 8th of 71 at his position. John Gibson has taken 13 of the starts with a .862 and -7.6 GSAx. That split is how a team allowing so few shots still ends up 15th in goals against. The third is a 71.4% penalty kill, 26th and six points under the league average, which gives back much of what the 5-on-5 game earns.

Luck in close games is also running against them. Pts vs Goal Diff is -1.9, 27th, after five straight seasons when it was mostly positive, including +5.4 last year. The last ten games included one-goal losses to Vegas, St. Louis and Florida. The recent slide is real in the standings: 1-4-0 over the last five, with only 1.8 goals a game. The process behind it has not collapsed, though. Over the last ten the goal differential per game is actually better than the season mark.

The skater group grades out average, with C grades at forward and on the blueline. Lucas Raymond, Alex DeBrincat and Viktor Arvidsson supply most of the scoring, and rookie-aged Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård are driving play well in their minutes. The bottom of the lineup is thin. Michael Rasmussen has 1 goal and a -9, Ben Chiarot has 2 points in 20.4 minutes a night, and Dylan Larkin has appeared in only 10 of 21 games. Shooting luck should turn, and the net should improve if Tarasov keeps getting the starts, so the most likely path is a climb toward the middle of the conference. Whether that climb reaches the playoff line depends on the kill and on who plays in goal.

strengths.title: Shot suppression, finally
strengths.body: Detroit allows 24.4 shots a game, 4th-fewest, and holds an even share of 5-on-5 attempts. This franchise spent the previous five seasons at 46-49% Corsi. The xGF% of 50.8% is the best mark in its recent history, so this reads as a structural change rather than a hot month, and it is the base a recovery would be built on.

strengths.title: Tarasov has been elite
strengths.body: Tarasov has a .931 save %, +9.5 GSAx and two shutouts in seven starts, which ranks him 8th of 71 goalies. Seven starts is a small sample and some regression is likely. Even so, his work is the reason the team's combined GSAx is still positive, at +3.6, 11th, despite Gibson's struggles.

strengths.title: Wingers carrying real offense
strengths.body: Raymond (21 points, 9 on the power play), DeBrincat (72 shots, 57.8% xGF) and Arvidsson (8 goals) form a legitimate scoring core on the wings. DeBrincat and Finnie are both well above 55% in expected goals, so the top of the lineup is winning its minutes. They have simply been converting below their usual rate.

concerns.title: League-worst-tier finishing
concerns.body: A 9.2% shooting rate, 30th, is why 28.5 shots a game produce bottom-five scoring. Part of this is luck and should come back toward the league's 11.4%. Part of it may be structural, because the bottom six offers little. Rasmussen has 1 goal on 29 shots and Copp ranks 104th of 240 centers. Expect some recovery, but not all the way to average.

concerns.title: Gibson's starts are costing games
concerns.body: Gibson has made most of the starts with a .862 save % and -7.6 GSAx, and he ranks 59th of 71. Behind a defense that allows this few shots, that is the clearest single fix available. If the workload keeps going his way, the goals-against number will not reflect how well the team defends.

concerns.title: A leaky penalty kill
concerns.body: A 71.4% kill ranks 26th, six points under the league average. It echoes the 70.1% of 2024-25, so it may not be a fluke. In a season this tight at 5-on-5, giving back a power-play goal most nights is the difference between winning and losing close games.

trend.note: The record has slid, with a five-game losing streak in November and a 1-4-0 run over the last five that produced only 1.8 goals a game. Over the last ten, though, the goal differential per game is better than the season's, so the results are falling faster than the play.

weekAhead.headline: Two home games: a hot Boston, then a goalie-propped Islanders
weekAhead.body:
This is a light week with two home games, and they offer two different tests. Boston is 13-6-1 and 5th on the site. Its record leans on a 104.1 all-situations PDO, 2nd in the league, and 13% shooting. Underneath, the Bruins allow 28.1 shots a game, 22nd, so Detroit's shot volume should travel well. They also hold centers and defensemen well under expectation and give up more of their scoring to wingers, which is exactly where Detroit's offense lives.

The Islanders are 9-6-4 and 16th, a weaker team on paper than their record. They hold 48.7% of expected goals and 48% of attempts, generate only 25.5 shots a game (27th) and allow 28.8 (26th). Their results lean on A-grade goaltending at +11.9 GSAx, 3rd. That is a game Detroit should control territorially. It becomes a shooting-luck problem again if the Red Wings cannot beat a hot goalie.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit wingers vs Boston's soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Boston has held centers and defensemen well under expectation (ranks 5 and 2) but allows a larger-than-league share of its points to wingers. Raymond, DeBrincat and Arvidsson are the Wings' best route to goals in that game. Boston's high PDO says some of its defensive success is borrowed.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's kill vs a weak Islanders PP
keyMatchups.body: The Islanders' power play is 28th at 17.2%, which gives Detroit's 26th-ranked kill a rare soft matchup. At the other end, Detroit's 20.6% power play runs into an 85.9% kill that ranks 4th. Special teams should roughly wash out, leaving the game to 5-on-5, where Detroit has the edge.

keyMatchups.title: Out-shooting a hot Islanders goalie
keyMatchups.body: New York's goalies are +11.9 GSAx with a .911 save %. Detroit's 9.2% shooting has to start converting its volume edge against a team allowing 28.8 shots a game.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts in goal. Tarasov in both games would be a signal that Detroit is ready to let its best goalie match its improved defense.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 74 points understates this team. A club with an even share of attempts, top-five shot suppression and a positive team GSAx should not keep shooting 9.2% or losing close games at a 27th-ranked rate. I project something like 33-38 wins and 78-88 points. That would be a clear improvement on the pace, but still a fight to reach the playoff line in an Atlantic where five teams already sit well clear. Expect scoring to drift up toward 2.9-3.2 goals a game as the shooting percentage recovers.

The tight shot suppression looks sustainable, given how big a break it is from past years. Tarasov's .931 will come down some. The penalty kill and Gibson's save % are the two things that can keep the record stuck below the underlying play, and the kill has a history of being bad. Larkin's limited appearances are worth watching too: a full-time top center would lift a forward group whose depth at center is its weakest part.
swingFactors: Tarasov vs Gibson split of starts

confidence.note: 21 games: the shot and chance trends are strong signals, but both goalie samples are small.
